newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle firm late, set highs, feeders fall.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle firm late, set highs, feeders fall.

text.p: CME live cattle futures firmed late on expected strong live markets to set new contract highs in October and December just ahead of the close while feeder cattle remained pressured by higher corn futures, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.325 cents per lb higher to 0.250 lower with August unchanged at 67.650 cents and October ending 0.325 cents higher at 71.275, just off the new high of 71.325. Feeder cattle ended off 0.650 to 0.350 with August off 0.625 at 82.025 cents.

Live cattle found renewed support late on ideas packers will pay higher prices for fed cattle later this week. Packers have adequate cattle numbers now but will need cattle later as beef prices appear firm, traders said.

General rolling of August longs into back months ahead of first notice day limited the advance in August after falling early following the sharp setback in feeder cattle. The fairly large premium futures hold to cash also limited upside potential, they added.

ADM Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien bought August late while Cargill Investor Services and RBH sold, traders said. Cargill bought October while E.D.& F. Man bought December. Spreaders bought December and sold October. RBH spread long October/short August, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, there was general selling of August 68 calls. Commercials sold December 74 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures ended lower on gains in corn futures and expectations the cash feeder market may have topped, as evidenced by a mostly lower trend in the CME feeder cattle index recently, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was down $0.05 at $82.12 per cwt.
FIMAT Futures USA sold August late while R.J. O'Brien bought. Smith Barney sold early while Lind-Waldock bought. Cargill spread long August feeders/short December live cattle, pit sources added.
Boneless beef futures ended mostly higher with trimmings mostly lower. Speculators were buying boneless beef while selling trimmings, traders said.
Boneless beef futures showed firmness, partly from school lunch program buying, while fresh cash trimmings were $4 to $5 per cwt lower, they said.
Boneless beef futures closed 0.50 cent per lb higher to 0.20 lower with August up 0.50 at 101.50 cents, a new contract high. December and February also set new highs.
Beef trimmings futures ended 0.10 cent higher to 2.00 lower with August off 1.20 at 46.00 cents.
